newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Baesa plunges on bleak outlook.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Baesa plunges on bleak outlook.

text.p: Pepsi bottler Baesa nosedived 38.7 percent on the Argentine bolsa Friday on mounting fears regarding the company's grim financial outlook, dealers said.
"Nobody sees a way out for Baesa, which has already defaulted on loans, and there's even talk it might be trying to reduce its assets," one dealer said.

Traders, however, noted Baesa went untraded in Buenos Aires Thursday when it plunged on Wall Street, and the local stock was now catching up with its ADR which reeled another 21 percent Friday in New York.
Baesa, Pepsi's biggest bottler outside the United States, failed to pay $500 million in debt obligations due March 31.
The company has said it is undergoing a restructuring process and holding negotiations with creditors, and has no plans to file for bankruptcy.
Last July Pepsi took over operating control of Baesa, which according to some analysts is suffering from overexpansion.
In fiscal 1996 the company lost $452.4 million against a $44.8 million gain in 1995.
